explanations.answer: On the first day of the first month
explanations.explanation: That's the date. The LORD tells Moses, Israel's leader, “On the first day of the first month you are to set up the tabernacle, the Tent of Meeting.” A real date, not a vague 'sometime soon.' I think anybody who's ever been told 'we'll get to it eventually' would appreciate that.

explanations.answer: On the seventh day of the seventh month
explanations.explanation: Seventh and seventh has a nice ring to it, friend, but that's not the date here. The LORD tells Moses, Israel's leader, “On the first day of the first month you are to set up the tabernacle, the Tent of Meeting.” First day, first month. No waiting around for the seventh.

explanations.answer: On the tenth day of the first month
explanations.explanation: You've got the right month, friend, just the wrong day. The LORD tells Moses, Israel's leader, “On the first day of the first month you are to set up the tabernacle, the Tent of Meeting.” So the day is the very first, not the tenth. That's nine days of difference, and you can bake a LOT of cookies in nine days.

Holy is the word. The LORD says to Moses, Israel's leader, “Take the anointing oil and anoint the tabernacle and everything in it; consecrate it along with all its furnishings, and it shall be holy.” The oil goes on, and the whole place and everything in it is set apart. It's like stamping every cookie in the batch, except nothing gets missed.

Close in spirit, friend, but that's not the word the LORD uses. He tells Moses, Israel's leader, to anoint the tabernacle and all its furnishings, and then says, “…and it shall be holy.” The anointing sets it apart. The word is holy.

I'm sure it was a sight, friend, but the LORD never uses that word here. He tells Moses, Israel's leader, to anoint the tabernacle and everything in it with the oil, and says, “…and it shall be holy.” The word he gives is holy, and it's about being set apart. Looks aren't in the verse.

True! The LORD tells Moses, Israel's leader, “Anoint the altar of burnt offering and all its utensils; consecrate the altar, and it shall be most holy.” Notice the step up. The tabernacle and its furnishings shall be holy, and this altar shall be most holy. Good ear, baker.

This one's true, friend, so False slips past. The LORD tells Moses, Israel's leader, “Anoint the altar of burnt offering and all its utensils; consecrate the altar, and it shall be most holy.” Most holy, not just holy. That's one step up from what he says about the rest of the tabernacle.

Water it is. The LORD tells Moses, Israel's leader, “Then bring Aaron and his sons to the entrance to the Tent of Meeting and wash them with water.” Aaron is Moses' brother. Before the garments and the anointing, there's a washing. Think of it like clean hands before you touch the dough.

Oil is in this passage, friend, but it's not the washing. The LORD tells Moses, Israel's leader, to bring Aaron, Moses' brother, and his sons to the entrance and “wash them with water.” The anointing comes after, in the verses that follow. Water first, then oil.

No wine in this scene, friend. The LORD tells Moses, Israel's leader, to bring Aaron, Moses' brother, and his sons to the entrance and “wash them with water.” Plain water, nothing fancy. Even in my bakery, the thing that gets used for washing up is water.

explanations.answer: So he may serve the LORD as a priest
explanations.explanation: That's the reason the LORD gives. He tells Moses, Israel's leader, to clothe Aaron, Moses' brother, with the holy garments, anoint him and consecrate him “so that he may serve Me as a priest.” The garments and the oil are for service. I think that makes it a pretty big job.

explanations.answer: So he may lead Israel into battle
explanations.explanation: Battle isn't mentioned here, friend. The LORD tells Moses, Israel's leader, to clothe Aaron, Moses' brother, with the holy garments, anoint him and consecrate him “so that he may serve Me as a priest.” The reason is priestly service. Holy garments aren't built for a battle, so I'd say this is a different kind of job.

explanations.answer: So he may judge the people's disputes
explanations.explanation: Judging disputes isn't in this passage, friend. The LORD tells Moses, Israel's leader, to clothe Aaron, Moses' brother, with the holy garments, anoint him and consecrate him “so that he may serve Me as a priest.” The reason the LORD gives is priesthood. That's the whole answer.

Right on. The LORD says, “Their anointing will qualify them for a permanent priesthood throughout their generations.” Permanent, generation after generation. This isn't a one-batch job, baker. It's meant to last.

Forty years isn't a number the LORD gives here, friend. He says of Aaron's sons, “Their anointing will qualify them for a permanent priesthood throughout their generations.” Permanent means no expiration date. I've had cookie recipes last longer than forty years, but even that's nothing next to this.

This one's bigger than Aaron, friend. The LORD says of Aaron's sons, “Their anointing will qualify them for a permanent priesthood throughout their generations.” So it reaches past Aaron and his sons, down through their generations. Permanent means permanent.

Second year is right. The text says, “So the tabernacle was set up on the first day of the first month of the second year.” That matches the first day of the first month the LORD named. Moses, Israel's leader, did it right on the day.

Fortieth is a long way off, friend. The text says, “So the tabernacle was set up on the first day of the first month of the second year.” Second year, not fortieth. Moses, Israel's leader, wasn't waiting four decades to hang a curtain.

Seventh is a nice number, friend, but it's not this one. The text says, “So the tabernacle was set up on the first day of the first month of the second year.” Second year is the answer. Moses, Israel's leader, followed the LORD's date exactly.

A cloud! The text says, “Then the cloud covered the Tent of Meeting, and the glory of the LORD filled the tabernacle.” The work is finished, and the glory of the LORD fills the place. That's the moment all those careful steps were leading to.

No storm here, friend. The text says, “Then the cloud covered the Tent of Meeting, and the glory of the LORD filled the tabernacle.” It's a cloud, and the glory of the LORD fills the tabernacle. The verse doesn't mention any thunder.

Nothing about wind in this verse, friend. The text says, “Then the cloud covered the Tent of Meeting, and the glory of the LORD filled the tabernacle.” A cloud covers the Tent of Meeting. That's what the verse gives us.

Not quite, friend. The text says, “Moses was unable to enter the Tent of Meeting because the cloud had settled on it, and the glory of the LORD filled the tabernacle.” So Moses, Israel's leader, does not walk in. He set up every piece, and he's unable to enter. That's a long day.

False is right. The text says, “Moses was unable to enter the Tent of Meeting because the cloud had settled on it, and the glory of the LORD filled the tabernacle.” Moses, Israel's leader, just finished the whole job and he can't go in. The cloud has settled on it.

explanations.answer: They set out on their journey
explanations.explanation: That's it. The text says, “Whenever the cloud was lifted from above the tabernacle, the Israelites would set out through all the stages of their journey.” The cloud lifts, and the people move. They know when to go by watching it.

explanations.answer: They bring offerings to the altar
explanations.explanation: Offerings are in this chapter, friend, but they're not what happens when the cloud lifts. The text says, “Whenever the cloud was lifted from above the tabernacle, the Israelites would set out through all the stages of their journey.” A lifted cloud means the Israelites set out.

explanations.answer: They gather to hear Moses speak
explanations.explanation: No gathering is mentioned here, friend. The text says, “Whenever the cloud was lifted from above the tabernacle, the Israelites would set out through all the stages of their journey.” When the cloud lifts, they set out. Moses isn't mentioned in that verse.

Fire, yes. The text says, “…and fire was in the cloud by night, in the sight of all the house of Israel through all their journeys.” A cloud by day, fire in the cloud by night. And everybody in Israel could see it.

Lightning is a good guess, friend, but it's not the word. The text says, “…and fire was in the cloud by night, in the sight of all the house of Israel through all their journeys.” Fire is what's in the cloud at night. Lightning comes and goes, and this was there through all their journeys.

I love a night sky, friend, since I keep one over my bakery. But the text says, “…and fire was in the cloud by night, in the sight of all the house of Israel through all their journeys.” The word is fire, and it was in the cloud. Starlight isn't in the verse.
